questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The true story of the 1969 Moon landing
How to talk to people who believe online conspiracies
Why Bill Gates is funding so much vaccine research
How fact checkers at the BBC do their job each day
questions.why: Sam says they'll hear advice on how to talk to people convinced by online conspiracies.

questions.q: Why does Neil mention the Moon landing, JFK and giant lizards at the start?
options: He is reading a history book about the 20th century
He wants to test Sam's general knowledge with a quiz
He has studied these events at university for years
He is pretending to have fallen for conspiracies
questions.why: Sam jokes that reading online conspiracies has sent Neil 'down the rabbit hole'.

questions.q: Why do people look for more information in times of crisis?
options: They feel uncertain and afraid and want to feel safer
They suddenly have more free time to read the news
Their governments tell them to research the facts
They want to become famous online by sharing posts
questions.why: Neil says as people feel uncertain and fearful, they look for information to feel more secure.

questions.q: According to Marianna Spring, why has Bill Gates become a target?
options: He made a big public mistake in a TV interview
He secretly works for the American government
He is rich and powerful and has funded vaccine work
He has spoken out strongly against all vaccines
questions.why: She says he's rich and powerful and has funded research into vaccines.

questions.q: How does Marianna Spring think we should treat claims about microchips?
options: Investigate them carefully
With the disdain they deserve
Share them to warn others
Report them to the police
questions.why: She says the ideas have no evidence and 'we should treat them with the disdain they deserve.'

questions.q: What does Dr Jovan Byford think is important?
options: Arguing strongly until the person gives up
Ignoring people who believe conspiracies
Blocking conspiracy websites
Separating the belief from the person who holds it
questions.why: He thinks it's important to separate the conspiracy from the theorist.

questions.q: Which piece of advice is part of Dr Byford's approach?
options: Try to find the real concern behind the belief
Tell them clearly that they're wrong
Avoid giving them any facts
Force them to change their mind
questions.why: Spring says to get to the bottom of the often legitimate concern at the heart of the conspiracy.

questions.q: Why does Sam say some conspiracies are dangerous?
options: They cost people a lot of money on fake cures
They make people stop trusting the BBC and its news
Believing vaccines kill could make the pandemic worse
They cause serious arguments inside many families
questions.why: Sam says people thinking vaccines will kill them might worsen the coronavirus situation worldwide.
